newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Mirvac group wins Olympic site bid.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Mirvac group wins Olympic site bid.

text.p: The New South Wales government said on Friday it had selected the Mirvac Village Industry Consortium to build the A$470 million athletes village for the 2000 Sydney Olympics.

New South Wales premier Bob Carr said the consortium, which includes Mirvac Ltd, CSR Ltd, James Hardie Ltd, Lend Lease Corp Ltd and Westpac Banking Corp, would create the world's largest solar powered suburb and set an environmental model for future urban development.
The village would provide accomodation for 15,300 athletes and officials during the Olympics and between 6,000 and 7,000 athletes and officials during the paralympics.
Carr said the Mirvac proposal had been approved by the International Olympic Committee, Australian Olympic Committee, and the Sydney Organising Committee for the Olympic Games.

Carr said the state government's capital contribution had been reduced to A$50 million, to be paid in the year 2000, and was expected to be further reduced under a profit-sharing agreement that should return A$17 million to taxpayers.

In July the short list for the design, construction, maintenance and marketing of the village was narrowed to the Mirvac consortium and the Aurora Village Pty Ltd -- which included Stockland Trust Group, Multiplex Construction Pty Ltd, Daewoo Corp's Daewoo Engineering and Construction Australia Ltd, Macquarie Bank Ltd and National Australia Bank Ltd.
"The project will provide 2,200 jobs during construction and a further 1,600 jobs in a proposed commercial and high tech industrial area at the north end of the village site," Carr said.
The village would be located over 90 hectares of a 272 hectare site at Newington, which was purchased by the New South Wales government from the Royal Australian Navy.
Carr said that after the Olympics, the village would become a Sydney suburb with 1,600 dwellings housing an estimated 5,000 people.
